whatThisIs: Three captures of the real running example (npm run demo -- --family-trip), taken by its own browser check. Everything shown about the family and the shops is invented example data; the kits, totals, dates and the repair were computed by the existing planner and solver during the run.
invented: The family (Rowan and Ash, adults; Wren, a child; "House of Alder"), the $60 reported progress, the weekly offers ($20 and $10), the kit list, both shops (sample-shop-one.example and sample-shop-two.example, a reserved name that cannot exist), all six "Sample:" listings, their prices, listed weights and stock, and the one-item-per-listing counts recorded as Rowan's. None is a real product, price, shop, person or family.
notShown: No live Channel3 search, OpenAI reading or Cohere ordering: none was called, and the last two are off in the example. No PayPal transaction. No human playtest and no physical device.
environment: Playwright 1.64.1 / Chromium 156.0.8078.4 headless, macOS arm64 with SwiftShader, reduced motion. The phone capture is the 390 x 844 touch-emulated project at device scale 2, not a physical phone.
clock: The server's day was pinned to Nov 8, 2026 (the worked example in docs/KIT-PLANNER.md), so the goal date is Dec 27. Started normally, the example uses the real day and a date seven weeks ahead.

solver.engine: native (compiled Rust), required for the run (KIT_SOLVER_REQUIRED=1)
solver.provenance: Not built in this checkout: no Rust toolchain is installed here. It is a copy of the existing build in the reviewed runtime worktree at b21b2d8, whose five solver sources are byte-identical to this commit's (hashes below). The hosted check builds it from source with the pinned compiler.

spec: test/e2e/family-trip.spec.mjs — a visitor tries a one-off expense, sees the real planner repair the kit, and makes one simulated contribution
command: Captured by the spec during the guarded run of the twelve affected spec files: KIT_SOLVER_REQUIRED=1 npx playwright test --config <the repository config with the test server probed at 127.0.0.1> ... --project=desktop --project=phone, with a minimal environment, OUR_CASTLE_ENV_FILE=none and the corrected Node TCP/fetch preload denying non-loopback transport. The page's own requests outside its origin are refused and counted by the spec.

images.shows: Step 4 of the spec: after the visitor types a $90 one-off and presses Compare complete kits. Two kits of invented "Sample:" listings fit by Dec 27: $150 (finishes Dec 20) and $180 (finishes Dec 27).
Step 6: the $180 kit is chosen with its stove kept, and the one-off is changed to $120. One kit fits: $150, the smallest change, switching only the tent; the stove is marked kept.

images.view: phone project, 390 x 844 touch-emulated at device scale 2
images.shows: Step 6 on the 390 px phone project: the same $150 smallest change, the switched tent, the kept stove, and the note that the listings are invented.

transportLimits: The preload is not an OS firewall: direct DNS, UDP and arbitrary child-process network APIs are outside its scope. The browser test separately intercepts requests outside its own origin. Earlier mutation probes did not load this preload and are not capture-isolation evidence.
